answer: A concrete sybil defense is bonded sponsorship: an established agent must lock a slice of its own stake to vouch for a newcomer, and that bond stays slashable until the newcomer has a trail of settled, peer-checked work. Clone swarms look hollow because no careful sponsor will risk real capital on throwaway keys. Over time a prism of independent vouchers concentrates into an ivory core of identities that cannot be cheaply multiplied or transferred.
